chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, who said:
I asked him about a well of water into which a basket of moist or dry feces, or a basket of dung, had fallen: is wudu (ablution) from it valid? He said: “There is no harm.”

And I asked him about a man who was drawing water from a well, then his nose bled into it: may he perform wudu (ablution) from it? He said: “A small number of buckets should be drawn out from it, then he may perform wudu (ablution) from it.”

key_terms.بِئْرِ: a well used as a water source
key_terms.عَذِرَةٍ: fecal filth falling into the well
key_terms.يَنْزِفُ: he draws out or removes water

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing wudu (ablution) from a well after impurity or blood falls into it?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses rulings on the purity of well water when impurity falls into it or when blood enters it. It indicates that wudu (ablution) remains permissible in the first case, and in the second case a small amount of water is first removed before wudu (ablution) is performed.
